author: WP18
summary: Updated-for-d6e9ff05 chapter on the cross-platform contract: the axes a CNA program is composed from, what IPlatform owns, the seven implementations and reserved values, renderer needs versus platform capabilities, audio independence, the target taxonomy and platform claims as evidence vectors. Mostly current; the Linux implementation list, the Win32 DPI ownership and the Android evidence line were stale. The Development platform pages already carried the backend mechanics; the composition, host-ownership, taxonomy and evidence-per-route material now lives on a new deep dive.

figures.note: Redrawn as text: four configuration inputs into CMake admission gates, one binary, then execution and oracle evidence per exact route.

sections.heading: Target taxonomy is still useful, but different
A platform claim is an evidence vector

concepts.text: A running CNA program composes five separately chosen inputs (target OS and toolchain, one platform implementation, a compiled renderer set with one active renderer, one audio implementation, and the XNA-shaped framework surface); they are composed, not collapsed into one backend name.

Each axis has its own selector and marker: the toolchain (CNA::TargetPlatform, CNA_TARGET_*), CNA_PLATFORM (default SDL3 on every OS, CNA_PLATFORM_<NAME>), CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER(S) plus GraphicsRendererSelection at run time, CNA_AUDIO_PLATFORM (SOUND_ENABLED for SDL3 and ALSA), and the framework headers (XNA namespaces, optional CNAEXT and the C ABI).

Separate axes make combinations such as HEADLESS+NULL+HEADLESS (server), SDL3 platform with NULL audio (deterministic graphics test), TERMINAL+SOFTWARE, SDL2 platform and audio, or native X11 with ALSA and no SDL ordinary configurations.
tokens: for a server or a test process

concepts.text: Not every product is buildable: configure refuses SDL2/SDL3 mixing, SDL-needing selections under CNA_ENABLE_SDL=OFF, GPU renderers under TERMINAL, host-exclusive values on the wrong host, renderer OS partitions and the reserved identifiers, by name and without fallback.
A refused combination fails at configure time with a message naming the missing package or capability, so it is configuration evidence rather than a later null window or a silent substitution.
tokens: refuses, by name and without fallback

target.evidence: cmake/PlatformSelection.cmake (FATAL_ERROR messages, no SDL fallback for X11/WAYLAND)

concepts.text: modules/platform owns CNA::Platform; the root IPlatform groups refcounted subsystem acquisition, window creation and adoption, batched event polling, counters/ticks/delay, input and system services, and the optional GL-context, Vulkan-surface and CPU-presentation bridges.

PlatformFactory::Create() is called once and its instance is never replaced; Create(name)/GetAvailable() exist because HEADLESS is always compiled (and TERMINAL off Windows) as a conformance reference; the ambient GetCurrentPlatform()/SetCurrentPlatform() serves the static XNA API and there is no environment variable that swaps implementations.

Public platform headers expose no SDL types; the toolkit is linked privately; a configure-time source ratchet rejects new SDL ownership outside the admitted boundary and a hot-path lint rejects platform calls inside per-pixel, vertex, sample and event loops.

Capabilities are read once and cached by the owning subsystem (calling GetCapabilities per frame is a defect), and PollEvents fills a caller-owned vector once per frame instead of per-event virtual dispatch.

The lifecycle preserves host ownership: production CNA never calls SDL_Init/SDL_Quit, acquires subsystems lazily through refcounted AcquireSubsystem, and ReleaseSubsystem of a never-acquired subsystem is a no-op so partial cleanup is safe while normal owners stay balanced.

SDL3 is the default implementation and the only one carrying mobile entry-point glue: Entrypoint.hpp renames main() at preprocessing time (SDL_main for Android's dlsym, UIKit start on iOS) and is empty under HEADLESS, TERMINAL and WIN32, which report managedEntrypoint false.
SDL2 is an independent implementation over real SDL 2.30 selected only on request, not SDL3 in a compatibility mode, and deliberately narrow.
tokens: not SDL3 in a compatibility mode

concepts.text: HEADLESS has no windowing dependency, is deterministic and stays compiled as a conformance reference even when another implementation is selected.
TERMINAL is a POSIX termios/poll implementation with terminal input and a CPU surface presenter, offered only on non-Windows targets and admitting only SOFTWARE, PORTABLEGL, HEADLESS and STUB.

SDL12 and EMSCRIPTEN are reserved and refused; WIN32 is refused off Windows and TERMINAL on Windows; X11 and WAYLAND are offered only when their development packages exist and refuse with a named diagnostic instead of falling back to SDL.

Targeting Emscripten with the SDL3 implementation is distinct from a native CNA_PLATFORM=EMSCRIPTEN backend (reserved); iOS and Android are target operating systems served by SDL3, not platform values.
tokens: is a different thing from a native

concepts.text: X11 owns Xlib windows and event translation, XKB keyboard with separate layout/repeat/modifier/composition paths, XIM preedit and commit, ICCCM clipboard, PRIMARY, XDND and INCR transfers, grabs and cursor modes, and derives DPI under an explicit policy (highDpi false by design).

X11 renderers consume a generic native handle and create their own GLX or Vulkan context/surface from the connection/window pair; link-closure and forbidden-reference gates prove the SDL-free boundary; automatic evidence runs under Xvfb, not on a real Xorg desktop.

Wayland keeps a window's wl_surface across hide and show but destroys and recreates the xdg role, because committing to an unconfigured role is a protocol error; configure serials, logical size and integer or fractional scale are tracked; EGL and Vulkan use the same native surface.

Wayland keeps keys (XKB) and text (text-input-v3) as separate streams with IME only for the focused window, uses data devices for clipboard and drag-and-drop and relative-pointer/constraint protocols for locked motion, turns missing optional globals into capability refusals, and is validated only by local Weston and Mutter campaigns (no workflow).
concepts.note: No-CI gap already recorded as NEW-B7-23.

target.evidence: modules/platform/src/Wayland/WaylandPlatform.cpp (capabilities); cmake/UnitTests.cmake (Wayland suites); no WAYLAND selection in .github/workflows

concepts.text: Win32 registers a window class, creates and pumps an HWND with stable identity, feeds raw input, converts UTF-16 at the boundary so public strings stay UTF-8, owns clipboard and IME; it reads the host's DPI awareness and never sets process DPI awareness itself (the older text said the platform owns DPI awareness).
concepts.note: Corrected: DPI awareness is process-global host policy; the backend reports coherent values for it.

concepts.text: MinGW/Wine proves the PE path and much of the Win32 contract; manual native-MSVC jobs and a recorded Windows-runner finding (a client-area size assertion that depended on screen size) add another tier; neither proves interactive IME, raw devices, multi-monitor or a physical GPU.

A renderer descriptor declares what it needs from the platform (needsWindow with a RendererWindowKind, needsGlContext, needsVulkanSurface, needsSurfacePresenter); CPU families present through IPlatformSurfacePresenter where surfacePresentation is reported; HEADLESS and STUB need none.

Some platform/renderer mismatches are refused at configure time and others when the device is created (for example a Vulkan family on a platform without a Vulkan surface), always as an error rather than a null dereference; the older text implied all are caught before factory invocation.
tokens: with an exception rather than a null dereference
concepts.note: Corrected scope: configure gates cover only part of the matrix.

concepts.text: Runtime selection does not relax the rules: every family in CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERERS must be admissible, the first GraphicsDevice latches the renderer, fallback happens only during initial creation when SetFallbackChain or EnableAutomaticFallback enabled it, and a live resource graph is never migrated.

CNA_AUDIO_PLATFORM implements SDL3, SDL2, NULL and ALSA; OPENAL and WASAPI are reserved and refused; ALSA is Linux-only, loads libasound at run time and mixes with CNA's own mixer instead of SDL3_mixer.

Audio is deliberately independent of the window platform (terminal or headless programs may use SDL3 audio, SDL3-windowed ones may use NULL); only SDL3 and ALSA define SOUND_ENABLED, and Windows and macOS have no SDL-free audio value, so an SDL-free WIN32 build is silent.
tokens: fully SDL-free WIN32 build is silent

concepts.section: Target taxonomy is still useful, but different
concepts.text: CNA::TargetPlatform (Desktop, Android, iOS, Web) is a compile-time classification of the build; getCurrentPlatformName() refines it to Web/Android/iOS/macOS/Windows/Linux/Desktop and DesktopOS enumerates Windows, Linux, MacOSX and Other; the CNA_TARGET_ prefix is kept apart from CNA_PLATFORM_ on purpose.

concepts.section: Target taxonomy is still useful, but different
concepts.text: Target values do not say which IPlatform, renderer or audio implementation was composed: Linux admits SDL3, SDL2, X11, WAYLAND, HEADLESS and TERMINAL (the older text listed only four), so 'the Linux renderer' is underspecified.
concepts.note: Corrected: native X11 and WAYLAND added to the Linux list.

concepts.section: A platform claim is an evidence vector
concepts.text: A platform claim is a vector of six separate facts: source path exists, configuration admits the combination, it compiles and links, it executes on a named host, the intended platform and renderer engage, and behaviour or pixels meet an identified oracle.

target.evidence: evidence method; applied to TARGET routes on the same page

concepts.section: A platform claim is an evidence vector
concepts.text: Later steps never follow from earlier ones: a descriptor compiles while its driver is missing, a PE runs without the intended translation DLL, a browser test proves DOM without pixels, and a HEADLESS conformance test does not exercise SDL.

concepts.section: A platform claim is an evidence vector
concepts.text: Per route at this snapshot: Linux has the strongest automatic evidence but only under Xvfb with software drivers; Windows automatic evidence is the Win32 harness under Wine with manual MSVC lanes; the web has the HTML_DOM Chromium suite and a bundle link; Apple lanes are declared; Android has no automatic evidence (the older text called it emulator-scoped).
concepts.note: Corrected: Android emulator records concern an earlier revision; no route is exercised automatically.

concepts.section: A platform claim is an evidence vector
concepts.text: The platform architecture makes routes easier to compose and test but does not retroactively promote older compile evidence into execution, hardware or oracle evidence.

issues.text: The full engine has no automatic Windows build or run; only the Win32 platform harness is cross-built and run under Wine, and all MSVC lanes are manual.
